Image F · Manual (current version V4.9.1)

Designed by 老F · Free to use, no commercial use (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0) · 中文说明

Image F (formerly “MJ还原工具”) lets GPT fix the errors in a Midjourney image — extra fingers, broken joints, seams, black bars — and then brings back the original's colour, tones, blur and grain, which GPT always changes. From V4.9 it is bilingual: choose the language when installing and switch any time at the bottom left of the tool. This manual describes the current version only. It is a single offline file; the “Copy” buttons next to the prompts copy them directly.

1. Install & start2. Workflows3. The five pages4. Prompts5. Upload order6. FAQ7. License & credit

1. Install & start

  • Install: double-click ImageF_V4.9.1_Setup.exe (one file, about 140 MB). First choose the interface language (English / 简体中文 — you can change it later in the tool), then follow “Next”. You can choose the install folder (default C:\Users\<you>\Image F, or e.g. D:\Image F; do not choose C:\Program Files — it is not writable, so generated images could not be saved). No admin rights needed. At the end you can tick “Open Image F now” and “Create a desktop shortcut”.
  • Blocked on first start: if the black window says Automatic setup was blocked, security software or a company policy stopped the automatic setup. From V4.9.1 the tool then opens a short help file and starts the Python 3.10 installer: click “Install Now”, then “Close” when it says “Setup was successful”, and Image F opens by itself. If no installer appears, double-click python-3.10.11-amd64.exe in tools\runtime inside the install folder, then open “Image F” from the desktop again.
  • If Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”: click “More info” → “Run anyway” (Image F is a free tool by 老F without a paid code-signing certificate; this warning is normal).
  • Opening it later: “Image F” on the desktop or in the Start menu (purple “IF” icon). The window opens large; the focus map and comparison images always fit the window and grow when you enlarge it. Layout: on the left, navigation for the 5 pages (1 Generate prompt / 2 Restore / 3 Calibration / 4 Style only / 5 Character sheet). On every page, images go on the left, settings on the right (the main button sits at the bottom of the settings and is greyed out with “Missing: …” while an image is missing), and results below (buttons such as Open / Copy are on the right of the result's title bar, the legend below the result). Hover over ⓘ for explanations; “How to use this page” at the top right opens this manual. The log is folded into the status bar at the bottom; click “Log” to open it (it opens by itself on errors). While processing, the result box shows progress and the status bar shows the latest log line. Generated images are saved in the Output folder of the install folder (the Start menu has an “Output folder” shortcut). Switching language: click 中文 (in the Chinese interface: English) next to “Manual · About” at the bottom left; the tool reopens itself.
  • Upgrading: install the new version into the same folder to upgrade (an old “MJ还原工具” install is found automatically, e.g. E:\MJ还原工具, and the folder name stays; old desktop / Start-menu shortcuts are replaced by “Image F”). Your calibration data is kept. When upgrading from V4.8 or older, the old 输出 folder and its images stay where they are and new results go to Output; settings such as the outfit description and face brightness are carried over. Uninstalling: “Uninstall Image F” in the Start menu or Windows Settings → Apps; you are asked whether to also delete the output images and calibration data (default: keep).
  • You can also use the folder without the installer: double-click ImageF.bat in it (on a PC that already has it set up, double-clicking ImageF.pyw works too; if the default Python isn't 3.10, it switches to 3.10 automatically). No need for “Run as administrator”, and no command line.
  • On a new PC the first start checks everything automatically: without Python 3.10 it installs the bundled one (for the current user only); missing numpy / OpenCV / Pillow are installed automatically (preferring the offline files in tools\runtime); broken installs are repaired. After that, double-clicking opens the tool directly.
  • If the setup fails, the window offers “Retry” and “Open log”; the log is tools\setup.log.
  • Don't double-click the .py files in tools directly (they need arguments and close immediately). When copying to another PC, always take the whole tools folder.

2. Workflows

Fixing errors (fingers, limbs, seams, black bars)

1 Page ①: drop in the MJ original → click “Measure & generate prompt” (copied automatically)
2 GPT: upload “Image 1” as shown in the “Next” bar at the bottom of page ①, paste with Ctrl+V in the same message, send; download the PNG
3 Page ②: drop in the GPT output → click “Start restoring” to bring back MJ's colour, blur and grain

The default prompt version is v4; if GPT sharpened motion-blurred passers-by or a blurred foreground, redo the same image with v4-B.

Fix + new head (replace the main character's head with a given character)

1 Page ①, “This time” on the right: choose Fix + new head; drop the MJ original into the left box (@图片1) and the character reference into the right box (@图片2, ideally the front portrait or 4-view sheet made on page ⑤) → click “Measure & generate prompt”
2 GPT: upload the MJ original (or the pre-compensated image) first, then the character reference, paste with Ctrl+V in the same message, send; download the PNG
3 Page ②: drop in the GPT output (“What GPT did: New head” is preset) → “Start restoring”: the new head's looks come from GPT, while hair colour, skin tone, lip colour, lighting and softness are restored from the old MJ head; body and background get MJ's colour, blur and grain back by position

Prompt = head-swap base prompt (error-fix rules + HEAD REPLACEMENT: face shape, features, hairstyle and hair colour from @图片2; head angle, expression, gaze, neck, body and lighting from @图片1) + the MEASURED LOOK measured from the MJ original, plus a final line: the measurements describe @图片1's light, colour grade, focus and grain, and the new head should be rendered in them too, but hair colour and features follow @图片2 — don't let the old hair colours listed above pull them back.

Fix + new character (head, body, outfit and shoes become the reference character; pose, lighting and composition stay)

1 Page ①, “This time”: choose New character; left box MJ original (@图片1), right box character reference (@图片2, a 3-view / 4-view sheet, ideally full body with shoes) → click “Measure & generate prompt”
2 GPT: upload the MJ original first, then the character reference, paste with Ctrl+V in the same message, send; download the PNG
3 Page ②: drop in the GPT output (“What GPT did: New character” is preset) → “Start restoring”

Prompt = character-swap base prompt (FULL CHARACTER REPLACEMENT: head, body proportions, outfit and shoes all from @图片2; pose, limb angles, gestures, head angle, expression, gaze, camera and composition from @图片1) + the MEASURED LOOK measured from the MJ original, plus a final line: the measurements describe @图片1's light, colour grade, focus and grain and the new character should be rendered in them too, but hair colour, skin tone, outfit and shoes follow @图片2 — don't let the old person's colours listed above pull them back.

When restoring (page ②, “New character”): the bundled depth model separates the whole person (hair, skin, clothes) from the background (if the person stands against a wall and depth can't separate them, colour is used instead). The area of new + old person is not compared by position (the old person's outline, bare shoulders or old clothes are not “printed” onto the new one). Hair, skin and lips are restored from the matching regions of the original MJ person (as with head swaps, a very different colour is treated as the character's own and not forced; skin only gets the colour grade, and how bright the face is is set by “Face brightness follows MJ” on page ②, see below). Clothing colour follows GPT (the new clothes have no counterpart in MJ, so only the global grade applies), while clothing softness follows MJ's old clothes (edge blur is matched; softened only, never sharpened).
Measured (the white-haired night scene, new character in a red plaid shirt): hair GPT L61 b+5.6 → MJ white hair L80 b−3.0, skin and lips follow MJ; the red plaid stays red plaid, its edge softness matches the 0.96 of MJ's black lace; no ghost of the old person around the figure. On 12 calibration pairs (where GPT did not swap anyone) it behaves normally, on average only 0.5–3 (out of 255) away from a normal restore.

Restore head-swapped images on page ② (“What GPT did” = “New head”), not with “Same scene redrawn / matched regions” on page ④. Those page ④ modes are for images with a different composition: “Same scene redrawn” grades by depth, which leaves a dark rim where a near person meets a far wall; “matched regions” can't recognise hair and skin in night portraits like these (it took a yellow wall for skin) and the colours end up far off. With “Auto (recommended)” on page ④, images with the same composition automatically take the same path as page ② and also recognise page ①'s head / character swap records. The same applies to full character swaps.

Character sheet (page ⑤)

A Front portrait: upload the MJ original (@图片1), paste prompt A, ratio 3:4; generate a few and pick the most faithful, most frontal one
B 4-view sheet (landscape): upload the front portrait first (@图片1), then the MJ original (@图片2), paste prompt B, ratio 21:9
C (optional) Page ④ “Style only”: MJ style image = the MJ original, GPT image = the 4-view sheet, to bring MJ's colour grade back

3. The five pages

Every place where you choose an image is a dashed rounded box: drag an image into the box from Explorer, or click the box to choose a file (png / jpg / webp / bmp / tif). If you drag several at once, the rest fill the following empty boxes on the same page (except the optional “Mask” box and greyed-out boxes not used in the current mode; drop a mask directly onto its own box). Once an image is in, the box shows the whole thumbnail with file name and size below; click the image to replace it, or × at the top right to clear it.

① Generate prompt (before GPT; with optional head / full character swap)

PurposeMeasures the colour, focus and grain of the MJ original and builds “generic error-fix prompt + MEASURED LOOK measurements”. With “Fix + new head” or “Fix + new character”, the base prompt switches to the matching version; the MEASURED LOOK is still measured from the MJ original.
InputThe “MJ original (= @图片1)” box (use the PNG downloaded from the MJ website). For a 2×2 grid, click “2×2 grid? Split into 4” below the box first, then click the cell to fix.
The “Character reference (= @图片2)” box on the right is only active for “Fix + new head” or “New character” (greyed out for “Fix only”): for a head swap, the head to put in (the front portrait or 4-view sheet made on page ⑤); for a full character swap, a 3-view / 4-view sheet, ideally full body with shoes (the prompt tells GPT to follow the front / clearest view). You can generate the prompt without it; the status bar reminds you to upload it.
OptionsIn the settings panel on the right. This time: Fix only (default) / Fix + new head / New character (head, body, outfit, shoes).
Prompt version: for “Fix only”, v4 (recommended, default) / v4-B / v3.3 (previous version, for comparison); for head swap “Head swap v1 (based on v4)”; for full character swap “Character swap v1 (based on v4)”. When you switch modes, a prompt generated for the other mode is cleared so you can't copy the wrong one.
The “Pre-compensated image (experimental)” switch is off by default.
The prompts always say @图片1 / @图片2 (“image 1 / image 2” — the tool keeps this exact spelling so that apps which link images by upload order work without editing).
OutputThe prompt is copied to the clipboard and shown (a green “✓ Copied” appears in the title bar and the MEASURED LOOK line is highlighted); the focus map on the right (green sharp / yellow soft / red blur). The “Next” bar at the bottom lists which images to upload, in order (“Image 1”, “Image 2”; hover to see the file path; with the pre-compensated image, Image 1 says so). “Open folder” finds the image to upload, and “Go to ② Restore →” jumps there. Files are in the Output folder.

② Restore (after GPT)

PurposeBrings the image GPT fixed back to MJ's colour, tones, haze, blur, glow and grain.
Input“MJ original (reference)” (carried over from page ① after measuring and marked “From ①”; don't choose the pre-compensated image), “GPT output” (the downloaded PNG, not a screenshot), “Mask (optional)” (white = use GPT, black = keep MJ; usually not needed).
OptionsAll in the settings panel on the right.
Restore mode: Changed areas only (default) — closest to MJ when GPT changed little; Whole image — the whole GPT image with MJ's style transferred, sharpest, for big GPT changes.
Output size: Same as GPT (default) / Shrink to MJ size.
“What GPT did: Fix only / New head / New character”: for an MJ image whose prompt was made with head or character swap on page ①, this is preset (marked “Preset from ①”; you can still change it). For full character swaps see “2. Workflows” above.
“Face brightness follows MJ” (only active for head / whole character swaps; greyed out for “Fix only”): drag the slider (left end GPT, right end MJ) or type 0–100 in the box at the top right. 0% = keep the new GPT face's own brightness; 100% (default) = the face as bright overall as the original MJ person's; 50% is in between. It only changes the overall brightness and slight contrast of the whole face; the lit side, shaded side, facial shadows and make-up are all kept, so no hard light/dark line appears. Want a fairer face — move towards 100; less fair — towards 0. Warmth (yellowish / pinkish) always follows MJ. Invalid input returns to the previous value, values above 100 become 100 and below 0 become 0; the tool remembers your last value.
With “New head”:
· First the main character is separated in both images: a face model locates the face, the cheeks give the skin colour, the area above the forehead and the fringe give the hair colour, and then “hair”, “facial skin” and background are separated. The centre of the face (eyebrows to chin, out to the outer eye corners) always counts as face; only the outer ring is classified as hair or skin — by texture when the image is sharp enough (hair has fine strands, skin is smooth), by colour when the image is soft — with a smooth transition between hair and skin. So when off-white hair and a shaded cheek have similar colours, the cheek and the outer eye corners are not mistaken for hair and lifted.
· The area of new + old head is not compared by position — the new head differs from the old one in position, face shape and hairstyle, and comparing by position would print the old head onto the new head and the background (the cause of the dark rim at the hairline and darkened cheek edges before V4.5); the background in that area is estimated from its surroundings.
· The new head is restored from the matching regions of the old MJ head: hair to hair (tonal distribution, warmth, chroma, which side is lit and which is shaded; if the two faces' angles differ too much, only the overall colour); skin only gets the colour grade (overall brightness per “Face brightness follows MJ” above, warmth per MJ, while the light/shade modelling of the face stays GPT's own — eye sockets don't go dark, shaded sides aren't lifted); lips to lips; the softness of hair and skin also follows the old MJ head (softened only, never sharpened).
· If the new and old head's hair colour (or skin tone, lip colour) differ a lot, that is most likely the character's own colour (the prompt takes hair colour from @图片2), so the tool does not force it to MJ's and only applies the global grade; the log says so.
· The pair check ignores the head; not added to calibration.
Measured (the white-haired night scene): hair GPT beige L64 a+1.6 b+6.3 → MJ white hair L76 a−2.5 b−2.6, skin L68 b+8.8 → L79 b+3.2, lips also follow MJ; the dark rim at the hairline and the darkened cheek edges are gone; hair detail contrast drops from GPT's 0.5–0.8 to 0.3–0.5 (MJ 0.26–0.49).
Measured on three pairs: the share of the face box mistaken for hair dropped from 17–25% to 8–14% (what remains is mostly real hair hanging over the face); a brightness profile across the face keeps GPT's shape and is only shifted, so the shaded side and chin no longer get a hard light/dark line; the dark eye sockets of the bc87863e pair are gone. With “Fix only” the result is pixel-identical to the previous version.
“Auto-add to calibration” is on by default; it is greyed out for “New head / New character” (such results are not added).
OutputThe restored image, a three-panel comparison and a change map (red = changed by GPT, blue = outpainted by GPT), all in the Output folder (file names end in _restored, or _restored_full for “Whole image”). Restoring the same GPT image again saves _2, _3 — earlier results are never overwritten; if the GPT image has transparent areas, the result keeps the same alpha channel. While restoring, the result box shows “Restoring…” and the elapsed time and the status bar at the bottom left shows the log line being written (click “Log” at the bottom right for the full log); if it doesn't finish, the result box says why and the log opens. In “Comparison” at the bottom, a landscape comparison is shown side by side (larger; the file itself is unchanged); the buttons on the right of its title bar: Open restored image / Comparison / Change map / Show in folder.

③ Calibration (improves with use)

PurposeRecords every pair of “image given to GPT + GPT output” and works out GPT's consistent drift, used for the prompt's anti-drift lines and the pre-compensated image. Aim for 5 pairs or more. After a tool upgrade or a change in the calibration data, it is recalculated automatically the next time you measure.
InputUsually nothing to do (page ② adds pairs automatically). To add one manually: put “Image 1: sent to GPT” and “Image 2: GPT output” into the two boxes and click “Add this pair”.
Buttons“Overview” on the right shows the built-in base pairs and the pairs added on this PC. At the top left of the card below, switch between “Pairs / Results”: the results list each drift (median, share of pairs agreeing in direction, used or not, outlier pairs); per-pair details are in the log. On the right of the title bar: Recalculate, Remove last pair, Open calibration folder (tools\calib).

④ Style only (when the composition differs)

PurposeWhen the GPT image and the MJ image differ in composition, aspect ratio or content (4-view sheets, white-background character sheets, different framing / crop / background), transfers MJ's colour, style and texture onto the GPT image. When the two images have the same composition (structural correlation ≥ 0.80), it automatically uses the same position-based restore as ②.
Image type“Auto (recommended)” by default (the result is written on the first line of the log), or choose it yourself:
· Same scene redrawn (e.g. the same night scene from another angle, buildings moved): same content proportions → graded by depth layers (see the next row); sky, distant mountains and background are graded together, while highly saturated spots such as lanterns and flowers keep their own colour;
· Character-focused (both images have a large enough face, face height ≥ 8% of the frame): matched regions, plus lips coloured separately like MJ's lips (pupils are not handled separately: closed or half-open eyes are not detected reliably);
· Different composition: matched regions (see “How it works” below).
Same scene redrawn: by depth layers The older method used one tone curve and one set of softening parameters for the whole frame, treating far and near alike: distant mountains, the far shore or far pavilions that GPT drew too sharp and too dark couldn't be “pushed back” on their own, and global sharpening made the distance even sharper. Now:
① Estimate depth first: the bundled depth model (Depth Anything V2 Small, Apache-2.0, tools\depth_anything_v2_small_w16.onnx, 47 MB, works offline) estimates a depth map for MJ and GPT, split into 5 bands: sky / farthest, far, middle, near-middle, near; the two images' depths are aligned by percentile (“the farthest x% to the farthest x%”).
② Each band is matched to the same band of MJ: tone curve (the lifted haze and greyed shadows of the distance are restored here), colour cast in shadows / midtones / highlights, and saturation. The two far bands follow MJ fully; the nearer, the more the whole frame counts (differences up close are usually different content, e.g. an extra white curtain or lamp on one side): about 1/3 for the middle, 1/5 for near.
③ Hue-family fine-tuning within layers: in the far / middle / near layers, 8 hue families (red, orange, yellow-green, green, teal, blue, violet-blue, magenta) each move their hue angle and chroma towards the same family in the same MJ layer (inherent colours such as eaves, trees, lake surfaces) — only when both images have enough pixels, at most 12° of hue and ±20% of chroma.
④ Softening per layer: each layer compares structural contrast at 2–64 px scales (distant ridges and far pavilions live at 16–64 px); it only reduces, never sharpens, so a distance drawn too sharp is pushed back to MJ's level.
At the end the log lists per layer “shadows / midtones / chroma: GPT → result (MJ)”. Note: the “subject colour difference” in the log is a whole-frame average of shadows / midtones / highlights; because this path matches per layer, that number can be about 1 higher than with a uniform grade (moonlit scene 0.7 → 1.7). This is normal: pulling the whole-frame average back to MJ at the end was tried and brought it down to 0.65, but the per-pixel comparison got worse (distance colour difference 0.55 → 0.73), so it was not adopted.
Where near and far meet (blurred window frames, hair edges) both sides are blended, so no bright rims appear; if the depth model is missing or fails, it falls back to the uniform grade automatically and the log says so.
Measured: in a redrawn moonlit scene, distance midtones 36.9 → 40.3 (MJ 41.4), large-scale distance contrast (32–64 px) 2.12 → 1.70, middle detail contrast 0.87 → 0.71 (MJ 0.67), roof-tile chroma 15.4 → 13.8 (MJ 14.9). In 13 comparisons with a known answer (the same image mirrored and cropped as a “redraw”, then mirrored back and compared per pixel with MJ), 12 got closer to MJ overall (mean 2.83 → 2.61), distance colour difference 1.40 → 0.55, near 1.54 → 1.04, and structural-contrast errors dropped in far / middle / near. The portrait, lips, matched-region and same-composition paths are not affected at all (pixel-identical). Time: about 15–25 s at 1920 px wide, about 30 s for a 1536×2736 portrait image.
How it works (matched regions)Both images are split into regions: background (white, or a solid / gradient backdrop touching the frame edge; large walls or sky in photos may also count — the log then warns you, and if you want them graded like MJ too, turn on “Background follows MJ”), skin, hair, and the rest of the subject split by colour into 4–6 blocks. Then skin is paired with skin, hair with hair, similar colours with similar colours; a shared “style” (brightness, contrast, colour cast, saturation) is computed from all pairs, and each block gets part of its own difference on top, weighted by how reliable its pairing is; regions without a counterpart in MJ only get the shared style. Soft masks along the edges blend the regions, so there are no seams; skin has hue / saturation safety limits. Texture comes from the MJ subject: softening or slight sharpening, glow (capped), luminance and colour grain, with the grain size converted by the two images' face widths.
Input“MJ style image” (a whole grid or one cell), “GPT image”.
OptionsStyle strength slider 0–1, default 1.00 (linear: 0.5 is half the effect); “Keep pure black” switch off by default; “Background follows MJ” switch off by default: when off, the background is left completely unchanged; when on, the GPT background is recoloured like MJ's (e.g. MJ has a grey-blue backdrop, GPT a white one), with hair edges blended. Anti-greying protection is always on.
Regions / depth previewOnly detects the type and splits the image (a few to a dozen seconds), no result image. For Same scene redrawn it shows MJ's and GPT's depth layer maps: blue = far, green = middle, red = near (the log lists each layer's share); for other types it shows MJ's and GPT's region maps: same colour = matched, grey = background, dark stripes = no counterpart in MJ (shared style only), red = lips (character-focused). If a result looks wrong, check here first whether the split makes sense.
Output<name>_style_restored.png in Output\style_only (same size as the GPT image; a transparent GPT background stays transparent), a comparison (MJ | GPT | result | MJ regions | GPT regions; for a redrawn scene the last two are MJ depth | GPT depth) and metrics.json (with the region pairing table; for a redrawn scene with far / middle / near tone and chroma statistics and per-band parameters). Not added to calibration.
All files of this page (result, labelled comparison, metrics.json, region preview) are saved in Output\style_only, never next to the GPT image, with _2, _3 for duplicates; “Show in folder” opens it.
LimitsThe more the content differs, the more only the “shared style” can be transferred: e.g. a wooden table or street that isn't in MJ only gets the overall style. Scenes without faces (landscapes, crowds) are split purely by colour, so the effect is close to a global grade. Skin / hair detection may be unreliable for cartoon / game characters, but regions with similar colours are still paired correctly; if the face model doesn't recognise a cartoon face, lips are not handled separately. If GPT added an occluder (e.g. an extra bag strap over the clothes), the covered fabric is not restored. Vignetting is not transferred yet.
Limits of “Same scene redrawn”: the depth model gives relative, not real distances; with almost no depth (flat illustrations, close-ups against a wall) layering doesn't help much and the effect is close to a uniform grade. Distant objects that GPT added and MJ doesn't have (e.g. a lit pavilion on the far shore) can only be pushed back by MJ's overall haze, contrast and colour in the distance — they aren't removed or turned into what MJ shows. Near layers follow the whole frame, so large near differences (e.g. a big white curtain on one side) are not forced flat.

⑤ Character sheet

PurposeMJ reference → front portrait → landscape 4-view sheet (portrait on the left + front / 90° side / back faceless full-body views on the right).
UseThe three step cards at the top (A → B → C) say which images to upload and which ratio to use for each step; “Go to ④ →” on card C jumps to Style only. The “Copy” buttons for prompts A / B are on the right of their title bars. For a custom outfit, write it in the “Custom outfit” box on the right (Chinese or English) and click “Generate full prompt B”: the full prompt B is copied, the title bar shows a green “Outfit added” and the added paragraph is highlighted. The description is remembered.

4. Prompts

For v4 / v4-B, preferably use the version generated on page ① — the tool appends this image's MEASURED LOOK measurements at the end. Below are the generic parts without measurements; you can use them directly when the tool isn't at hand.
Fix v4 (default, recommended)Upload 1 image: the MJ image to fix = @图片1
Retouch @图片1 : find and fix EVERY error in it, then output the same picture with those errors corrected. Be thorough — a missed error counts as a failure. This is the same image repaired, not a new image.

FIX ALL OF THESE (mandatory, no exceptions):

• Every person in the frame, checked one by one — the main subject and also anyone small, distant, out of focus, motion-blurred, in shadow, at the edge, or partly hidden behind another person or object:
  – Hands and fingers: count the visible fingers; correct joints; no fused, extra, melted, or floating fingers; every hand attached to a wrist and forearm. A hand whose fingers are all in view — open, spread, or flat, with nothing covering them — must have exactly five: four fingers and a thumb; a missing or extra finger on such a hand is an error, so fix it. Fingers hidden by a fist, a grip, the other hand, an object, a pocket, or the frame edge, or lined up behind one another by the hand's angle, are not missing — never open a fist, unfold a grip, or expose hidden fingers just to show five.
  – Arms and legs: each connects to the right shoulder or hip and bends only at real joints. Crossed or folded arms must read clearly as one forearm in front of the other, with both hands accounted for. No limbs that merge, split, or pass through each other or the body.
  – Faces: eyes, nose, mouth, and ears in the right place and proportion; no doubled, smeared, or melted features.
• Structure: melted or fused objects, deformed shapes, straps, chains, or parts that end in mid-air or pass through each other.
• Physics: impossible gravity, balance, contact, or grip; broken perspective or scale; a single object whose shadow clearly contradicts the existing light (backlighting, silhouettes, and deep shadows are not errors — never re-light the scene).
• Artifacts: garbled text, fake logos, duplicated fragments, banding.
• Seams: any straight line where the two sides are offset, misaligned, or differently exposed — re-align the content and blend until the line disappears.
• Letterbox or pillarbox bars: perfectly flat, empty black or white bands running straight along the canvas edges — fill them by extending the scene at the same scale, perspective, light, focus, and grain, so the picture fills the whole canvas. Dark scene content at an edge (night sky, shadow, a dark wall or ceiling, vignetting) is not a bar — keep it as it is.

Blur, motion blur, shadow, haze, small size, background position, or partial occlusion is NEVER a reason to skip an error. Fix it inside the blur: rebuild the correct shape, then render it exactly as soft, streaked, dim, or translucent as that spot was.

STYLE LOCK — everything you did not fix must look identical:
1. Color: the same white balance, hues, saturation, contrast, and black level — not warmer and not cooler, not more and not less saturated. Do not re-light, de-haze, or re-grade.
2. Focus: soft, blurred, and motion-blurred areas stay exactly as soft. Never sharpen, de-blur, or add clarity or detail; a corrected part takes on the blur of its spot.

STYLE LOCK: match @图片1's medium and rendering exactly — whether it is a photograph, painting, illustration, anime, or 3D render — including its level of realism, line and edge quality, skin and hair texture, colour grade, softness, grain and mood. No crisp HDR sharpening, no clarity boost unless @图片1 has it.

FRAMING LOCK: tight close-up framed from just above the top of the hair down to the collarbones only. The collarbones sit at the bottom edge of the frame; nothing below the collarbones is visible (no chest, no shirt body, no pin badge). The face fills about 60% of the frame height and is centred horizontally. Do not crop the top of the head. Vertical portrait orientation.

POSE LOCK (absolute front view): the head is perfectly upright, level and facing straight forward, held vertical with the chin at a neutral height. The face is centred and symmetrical to the viewer: both ears equally visible, the nose on the vertical centre line, both eyes on one horizontal line, shoulders level and square to the viewer. Eyes look straight at the viewer at eye level, seen from an eye-level, straight-on viewpoint. Neutral relaxed expression, mouth gently closed. Every facial feature is individually seen in a perfectly frontal, level view: both eyes the same size and shape with irises centred and looking straight ahead, both eyebrows at the same height, the nose seen straight on with both nostrils equally visible and the bridge running vertically, the mouth level with both corners at the same height, both cheeks equally wide, and the left and right halves of the face equal in width. The lower face is symmetrical too: the chin point, the centre of the lips and the philtrum sit exactly on the same vertical centre line as the nose, and both sides of the jaw are the same length and angle. Rebuild every feature in this perfectly centred position, independent of the reference's camera angle, head turn or tilt.

ANATOMICAL RECONSTRUCTION: Before drawing, analyse the face in @图片1 as an anatomist would, from every angle it appears in. Work out the underlying skull and bone structure — forehead height, brow ridge, cheekbone width and height, jaw width and angle, chin length and shape — and the soft-tissue proportions: face length to width ratio, eye spacing relative to eye width, eyelid shape and fold, nose length, bridge and tip width, lip thickness and mouth width, and the distances between brows, eyes, nose, mouth and chin. Correct for the perspective, foreshortening and head tilt of each angle in @图片1, then rebuild exactly how this same face looks from a perfectly level frontal view. If @图片1 is stylised, keep its stylised proportions rather than making them realistic. Use only what @图片1 shows; where an area is hidden, infer it from the visible anatomy rather than from a generic or idealised face.

IDENTITY: Preserve the character's real face shape, proportions, skin tone, age and overall impression exactly as in @图片1, plus the same hairstyle, hair colour, earrings, necklace and collar. Do not beautify, idealise, or "correct" the face. Do not change their age or make them look more mature or more model-like. Do not enlarge the eyes, slim or lengthen the face, sharpen the chin, or add makeup that is not in @图片1. It must read instantly as the same character, not a lookalike or a new one.

FACELESS FULL-BODY VIEWS: in the three full-body views, the face is a smooth, blank, featureless surface like a tailor's mannequin, with no eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth or makeup, in the character's skin tone, keeping the correct head shape, jaw line and ears. Measure the body in head-heights using the left portrait's head: the total height is about 7.5 to 8 heads for a realistic adult (keep @图片2's proportions if it is clearly stylised). The chin sits at 1 head, nipples at about 2, navel at about 3, crotch at about 4 (the midpoint of the body), knees at about 6, feet at 7.5 to 8. The shoulders are about 2 head-widths wide and hands reach mid-thigh. The head in the full-body views must be the same size relative to the body as these proportions require — do not enlarge the head or shrink the body, legs or torso. Keep the body build consistent with @图片2.

NECK AND SHOULDER ANATOMY CHECK (all panels): do not copy a wide, long or muscular neck caused by a reference's camera angle, lens or pose. The neck is a slim, near-parallel column, clearly narrower than the jaw, never a wide trapezoid flaring toward the shoulders. The trapezius starts low and short, a gentle soft slope blending into the shoulders, not a tall steep ridge from behind the ears; for a slim or average build it is barely visible. The neck has a natural, moderate length, the collarbones are subtle and nearly horizontal, and the shoulders are level, relaxed and slightly sloped.

6. FAQ & tips

  • Page ④ lifts black clothes or tints them cyan: turn on “Keep pure black”; if still too bright, lower the style strength to 0.6.
  • Page ② says “the aspect ratios differ too much”: most likely the wrong image (not the same picture). The tool handles small crops, outpainting and shifts automatically; only click “Yes” to continue if you're sure.
  • Restoring didn't finish: the message says why. Most often “MJ original (reference)” and “GPT output” aren't the same picture — the tool stops on purpose, makes no misaligned collage and adds nothing to calibration; choose the right image and try again. It can also be an image or mask that can't be read (damaged or not an image). (Don't use the command line's --force.)
  • Restored, but adding to calibration failed: the saved restored image is not affected; the status bar says so separately and the reason is in the log.
  • Copying the prompt failed: when another program holds the clipboard, the status bar says “Copy failed”; click “Copy” in the prompt's title bar again in a moment.
  • The pre-compensated image was chosen as the reference: the tool switches back to its MJ original automatically.
  • GPT sharpened motion-blurred passers-by: redo with v4-B on page ①.
  • The full-body figures in the 4-view sheet still have facial features: replace “smooth, blank, featureless surface” in prompt B with “completely blank face, no facial features at all”. When generating video from a faceless 4-view sheet, state that the face follows the portrait on the left.
  • Images with a completely different composition (4-view sheets, character sheets): use page ④, not page ②.
  • Download GPT's images as the original PNG whenever possible — no screenshots.
